title: Standings table: no rank within each event is shown when results are saved
duplicate_check_notes: No bug data is available through a configured TestBench integration, so no comparison was made.

requirement_link.acceptance_criterion: The table shows the rank within each event, and also the total and the total position (user clarification of REQ-LOCAL-004).

environment.browser: Playwright MCP browser (Chromium-based, version not recorded)

preconditions: The app is running at http://localhost:8080/.
TP-Anna and TP-Cia each have 100m 11.00; TP-Bo has 100m 10.50 and Long Jump 700 cm.
steps_to_reproduce: Open the app and select the competition TP-AUD-20261105-01.
Look at the standings table, including the 100m and Long Jump columns, and hover the event cells.
Optionally click Export CSV and open the file.
Look for the rank of each competitor within the 100m event and within the Long Jump event.
expected_result: Each competitor has a rank within each event they have a result in, plus the total and total position. Source: REQ-LOCAL-004 as clarified by the user ("Placement per event means rank within each event; total and total placement are also shown").
actual_result: The table shows the total and the total position (Pos). Each event cell shows only the result and points, for example TP-Bo 100m: 10.5 s and 975. No rank within an event is shown in the table, in its HTML, on hover, or in the CSV export (columns: Position, Name, Competition, result and points per event, Total).

reproduction_rate.attempts: 2 of 2 (EX-007; EX-013 after a page reload and with the CSV export)

severity.rationale: A clarified requirement is not met, but totals, positions and points are correct and no data is lost. Severity is a proposal for human review.

agent_confidence.basis: The absence of an event rank is clearly observed and reproduced through three routes. Confidence is not High because the requirement text was clarified by the user and a design reference was not available; the UI may intentionally show only points per event.

proposed_manual_test.objective: Confirm with the product owner how rank within an event is meant to be shown.
steps: Review the requirement and design for event rank.
With three competitors holding different 100m results, check where the 100m rank is shown.
proposed_manual_test.expected_result: The agreed event rank is visible for each competitor and event.

title: Enter result: an unreasonable 100m value (99999 s) is accepted and saved without an error
duplicate_check_notes: No bug data is available through a configured TestBench integration, so no comparison was made.

requirement_link.acceptance_criterion: Negative, non-numeric, empty and unreasonable values for an event are rejected with a clear error message and the result is not saved (user clarification of REQ-LOCAL-006).

environment.browser: Playwright MCP browser (Chromium-based, version not recorded)

preconditions: The app is running at http://localhost:8080/.
Competition TP-AUD-20261105-01 (Decathlon) is selected with a competitor TP-Key that has no results.
steps_to_reproduce: Click the row TP-Key so that the competitor is loaded in Enter result.
Type 99999 in Result and click Save score.
Read the message, then reload the page, select the competition and look at the TP-Key row.
expected_result: The value is rejected with a clear error message and nothing is saved. Source: REQ-LOCAL-006 as clarified by the user (unreasonable values for the event are invalid).
actual_result: No error is shown. The status line says Saved: 0 pts, the 100m cell shows 1666:39 (99999 s), TP-Key gets position 6 and the server answered 200. The value is still there after a reload. In the same session, 0.5 s was rejected with Faster than the world record for 100m: 9.58 s, so an unreasonable low value is handled and an unreasonable high one is not.

reproduction_rate.attempts: 2 of 2 (EX-012 attempt 5 and EX-016); persisted after reload (EX-013)

severity.rationale: Invalid data is stored and shown in the standings (scored 0 points), but other clearly invalid values are rejected and the data stays contained in a test competition. Severity is a proposal for human review.

agent_confidence.basis: The behaviour is reproduced twice and persisted. Confidence is not High because no numeric upper limit for unreasonable values is defined; 99999 s (about 27.8 hours) is unreasonable under any reading, but the exact threshold is unspecified.

proposed_manual_test.objective: Find out which upper limits the app should enforce per event and check each event.
steps: Agree an upper limit per event.
For each event enter a value just below, at and above the limit.
Check message and that above-limit values are not saved.
proposed_manual_test.expected_result: Values above the limit are rejected with a clear message and are not saved.
